sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Whole-app container setup
sections.what: Describes both services together: their ports, shared folders, settings file, health check and start order.
sections.why: Likely reason: one file defines the whole multi-part setup. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: The backend folder is shared over the image, so the running code is whatever is on the host disk, not what was built into the image.

summary: Defines two containers, a backend on port 8000 and a frontend on port 3000, and how they run together.
purpose: Lets someone start the whole app with one command on any machine that has Docker.
why: Likely reason: running in containers makes the app behave the same on different machines. Reason not stated in the file.
how: The backend image is built from its folder and started on port 8000. The backend code, data and logs folders are shared into the container. Settings are read from the backend environment file. A health check asks the backend's health address every 30 seconds and restarts it after repeated failures. The frontend is built from its folder, given the backend address, served on port 3000, and started after the backend.
inputs: The backend and frontend folders with their Dockerfiles, and the file backend/.env.
outputs: Two running services reachable on ports 8000 and 3000, plus data and logs folders on the host.
risks: The ports are open on the host machine, so other computers on the network may reach them. The environment file holds keys and is read directly. The named data and logs volumes at the bottom are declared but not used, since folders are shared directly. The health check needs the curl program inside the backend image.
debug: If the backend will not start, check that backend/.env exists and that the backend Dockerfile is valid. If the health check keeps failing, confirm curl is in the image and the health address exists. If data is missing, check the data folder on the host.
